story.title: Lacquer the City Wall
story.text: Qin Er Shi wanted the wall lacquered bright. His ministers said it cost too much.
story.narration: The Records of the Grand Historian, in its chapter on jesters, tells it this way: Qin Er Shi had a new idea — to lacquer the whole city wall until it shone. His ministers told him what it would cost in money and in labour, and the more they said, the less he listened.

story.title: You Zhan Says: Splendid
story.text: You Zhan said: lacquered smooth, no enemy could climb it. It would just need a roof.
story.narration: You Zhan did not say it was a bad idea. He said: splendid! Lacquered slick, no attacker could get a handhold. Only, when it is done you would need a shed bigger than the wall to keep the sun off it — and where would anyone find a shed that size? Qin Er Shi laughed, and the wall was never lacquered.

keyMoment.question: Qin Er Shi is set on lacquering the wall and will hear no argument. What should You Zhan say?

options.text: Agree it is splendid, then point out the huge shed it would need
Say to his face that it wastes money, and count the cost line by line
options.hint: The more right he is, the more it feels like a challenge.

options.text: Write a long memorial listing every reason against it
options.hint: Every reason is sound, and the emperor will not even read it.

keyMoment.reveal: No names, no head-on fight — say it another way, and he takes it in himself.

misconceptions: To be heard you have to say it louder and louder
Pointing at the mulberry just means talking behind someone's back

quiz.question: How did You Zhan argue against lacquering the wall?
options: He called it splendid, then pointed out the giant sun-shed it would need
He said to the emperor's face that it cost too much
He asked the ministers to present a joint memorial
quiz.explanation: He never said it was wrong: he laid out the difficulty, and the emperor laughed and changed his own mind.

quiz.question: The classmate next to you keeps twirling a pen and you cannot follow the lesson. What is better to say?
options: After class: your trick looks great, but it makes me lose track
Shout in front of the whole class: stop twirling that pen!
Say nothing and move to the back row
quiz.explanation: Say it another way and he takes it in himself — speaking to the one who needs to hear beats speaking louder.
